description:
FOUND + FIXED s517b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-15).

REPRO: use IO::Compress::Gzip; my $gz; my $z = IO::Compress::Gzip->new(\$gz); $z->print("x"); $z->close; print length $gz  # perl 30; PCL 0, and files named SCALAR(0x1) appear in the cwd.

CAUSE: lib/PCL/Facts/IO/Compress/Base/Common.pm (#3205, s515a) listed `sub whatIs ($;$);`.  whatIs is not exported; its only callers are whatIsInput/whatIsOutput in the same module, ABOVE its definition, where perl applies no prototype.  The overlay is consumed at the module unit's package statement, so the prototype applied there.

FIX: the line removed from the overlay, with a why-comment.  The generic question (should a module's own unit apply its overlay positionally?) is NOT changed here: every other entry in that overlay is an exported sub whose in-module call sites follow its definition.

=== DONE (s517b) ===
subject: The IO::Compress::Base::Common facts overlay declared `whatIs ($;$)` -- not exported, and the module's OWN unit reads the overlay, so `whatIs(@_)` inside whatIsOutput passed @_'s COUNT and every output buffer `\$buf` became a FILENAME "SCALAR(0x1)"
